title: Cauliflower & Parsnip Puree
description: From Love & Lemons: This cauliflower & parsnip puree is like the fluffiest mashed potatoes you can imagine. Thanks to the parsnips and roasted garlic, it's rich, nutty, and delicious. This year, this puree is taking the place of the mashed potatoes at our Thanksgiving dinner. You might be thinking, “What?! That’s crazy!” You’re not alone. That’s what Jack thought too. He’s a big mashed potato purist. Last year’s cauliflower mashed potatoes were a stretch for him, so parsnip puree sans potatoes seemed pretty nuts. Well, good news! Both of us couldn’t stop eating the puree by the spoonful before it made it to the table. It’s rich and nutty, with an amazing light and fluffy texture. Mashed-potato-purist approved! Jack loved this recipe, and I think you will too.
ingredients: 5 medium parsnips (1 pound), peeled & chopped into 1-inch pieces (cutting around the wood interiors near the fat ends)
1 medium cauliflower (2 pounds), broken into small pieces, matching the parsnips
5+ cloves Roasted Garlic (roast the garlic in advance and store any extra cloves in the freezer.)
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, more for drizzling
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
directions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and boil the parsnips and cauliflower for about 10 minutes or until fork tender.
Drain well and transfer to a blender.
Add the roasted garlic to the blender along with the olive oil, lemon juice, ½ teaspoon of salt, and a pinch of pepper.
Blend, using the blender baton to push down the contents, and blend to a smooth consistency.
If necessary, add a bit of water or broth to get the blender moving, but do so sparingly so the puree doesn’t become too thin.
Taste and add the additional ½ teaspoon of salt, if desired.
Transfer to a serving bowl and stir in the rosemary while the mash is still warm. Add a drizzle of olive oil, more pepper, if desired, and serve hot.
